card.title: The Third Detail Matters
card.instruction: Choose one arbitrary detail and treat it as the key that explains, controls, or prevents the entire impossible situation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our ferry's floating above the harbour. Keep that souvenir pebble level; it's the only thing stopping us tipping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I picked it up for you. I need my hands for the bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it in my lunchbox. I'll keep the ferry level.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll flatten them into a level bed. Lunch can suffer; the passengers mustn't slide off.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns ferry stability to the pebble, A3 takes over its level support, and A5 deforms lunch to protect the supposed control point.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's bag-handling need causes A3's lunchbox solution; B4's sandwich tilt causes A5's flattening plan.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs both hands for luggage and B4 identifies the physical defect in A's proposed support.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's tilt observation to sacrifice the ordinary lunch rather than relinquish the pebble theory.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a ferry floating above the harbor and the exact pebble A treats as its stabilizer.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's lunch-versus-passengers choice follows B4's sandwich interference.

coach2.missing: No essential gap; actual causal power of the pebble is A's claim, not something the reader must independently verify.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; one arbitrary detail controls each practical response.
